title: Inject the diagnostic trace sink and remove core file creation
summary: Define a platform trace-sink contract, move host file creation and buffering for CPU tracing from rumiga-core into the desktop adapter, keep record formatting and bounds in the core, and make tracing available in both runtime profiles without changing the recorded bytes.
scope: Core trace ownership and public tracing API

risk.failure_mode: A changed record layout or a lost buffered write would silently invalidate existing CPU trace comparisons and capture-manifest trace counts.
risk.rollback: Revert the M1-004 platform, core, and desktop commits together to restore the file-owning core; no persisted data format or on-disk state depends on the new contract.

compatibility.detail: The core's public tracing API changes. enable_cpu_trace, the trace_writer and trace_limit fields, and the public trace_count field are replaced by set_trace_sink, flush_trace, clear_trace_sink, and a trace_count accessor. Desktop CLI behavior, trace file bytes, and the capture manifest trace_count value are unchanged.

security.detail: No network transport, credential, authorization, persistence, unsafe-code, or FFI behavior changes. Host path handling moves from the core to the desktop adapter without widening the set of reachable paths.

tests.proves: The desktop-selected core profile reproduces golden trace records captured from the previous file-writing implementation and honors the trace limit without creating a file.
The allocator-backed profile produces the same records, so tracing is portable rather than host-only.
The desktop adapter owns file creation, truncation, the newline terminator, and host error reporting.
The stock core graph still compiles with the declared Rust MSRV after the new dependency edge and contract.
Commit policy, lockfiles, governance, host checks, compatibility, supply chain, the portable RISC-V profile, and the ESP32-P4 firmware build all pass for the change.

evidence.location: 2026-08-17 local execution: the trace suite passes under both core runtime profiles with identical golden records, the desktop file transport suite passes, and the declared Rust 1.85 MSRV check passes.
evidence.proves: Byte compatibility and the removal of core file creation are locally valid before pull-request promotion.
